Data sources

Source: vignettes/articles/data-sources.Rmd
data-sources.Rmd

rendehR reads three intensive care databases from PhysioNet and their open demo versions. The source registry (rendehr-data-source.json, list_registered_sources()) holds each one’s release, tables and identifiers; register_source() adds a new one, see vignette("adding-a-new-source").

Source Name in rendehR Release Access Tables read
MIMIC-III mimic_iii 1.4 credentialed 26
MIMIC-IV mimic_iv 3.1 credentialed 31
eICU-CRD eicu 2.0 credentialed 31
MIMIC-III demo mimic_iii_demo 1.4 open 26
MIMIC-IV demo mimic_iv_demo 2.2 open 31
eICU-CRD demo eicu_demo 2.0.1 open 31

Credentialed sources need a PhysioNet account with credentialed access, the required training and the project’s data use agreement signed; download_source() then fetches them with your PhysioNet credentials. The demo sources (100 patients each for MIMIC, about 2,500 unit stays for eICU-CRD) are open to everyone and are what the articles on this site use. The registry also keeps definitions for HiRID, AmsterdamUMCdb and SICdb; they are blocked until their support is validated.

How the sources differ

MIMIC-III MIMIC-IV eICU-CRD
Hospitals one (Beth Israel Deaconess, Boston) one (Beth Israel Deaconess, Boston) more than 200 US hospitals
Years 2001-2012 2008-2022 2014-2015
Patient subject_id subject_id (uniquepid)
Hospital admission hadm_id hadm_id patienthealthsystemstayid
ICU stay icustay_id stay_id patientunitstayid
Time dates shifted per patient dates shifted per patient minutes from unit admission, no dates
Diagnoses ICD-9 ICD-9 and ICD-10 problem list and ICD codes
Deaths after discharge yes up to one year no (hospital only)

These differences reach every analysis:

  • Clock. rendehR expresses every time as minutes since hospital and ICU admission (time_since_hadm_min, time_since_icu_min), so the three sources share one clock. Calendar dates exist only in MIMIC, shifted per patient: intervals within a patient are real, absolute dates are not.
  • Level. MIMIC records data per hospital admission with ICU stays inside it; eICU-CRD is organised by ICU unit stay. merge_sources() merges at admission level (one row per hospital admission, first ICU stay) or at ICU level (one row per ICU stay); see vignette("harmonized-data").
  • Coding. Cohort definitions list both ICD-9 and ICD-10 codes, so one definition selects comparable patients in every source; see vignette("cohorts").
  • Content. Not every concept exists in every source (for example eICU-CRD has no post-discharge mortality). The concept dictionary shows which sources define each concept, and the explorer’s Availability tab shows how often a cohort actually has it.

Where the files go

download_source() stores each source as Parquet under the project’s raw data root, one folder per source (<raw_data_root>/<source>/). The files are read, never modified; the cohort import streams only the rows of the cohort into the database. Keep credentialed data where your data use agreement allows, and never publish individual-level rows.
